body_html:
Welcome to Midweek Movers! This is where I rank your favorite stocks from worst to first.

Today, I plan to buy the #2 and #1 ranked stocks during market hours.

So far in 2026, the winners from this series have averaged 25.9% returns, and more than 75% are still up today.

Subscribe now

I’ve been investing since 2007 and creating finance content for the past six years, with a focus on finding high-performance stocks. We also recently broke into the Top 100 Finance publications globally. Pretty cool!

Here are all 52 stocks we sorted through today:

Lets go ahead and get started, as this is our largest filtering of stocks ever…

Stock Price is Below the 200 Day Moving Average

Stocks trading below their 200-day moving average are automatically eliminated. I’m looking for stocks showing strength and capable of pushing toward new 52-week or all-time highs…not stocks stuck in long-term downtrends.

We don’t need to catch the bottom or try to catch falling knives. Let price action prove itself first.

Too Young of a Stock

Remember when we waited three years after Palantir’s, , IPO before getting interested? It went on to run 580%. More recently, I’ve advocated for patience with SpaceX rather than rushing in immediately after its IPO.

We do not need to be first.

With a newly public company, I’d rather have some chart history, several earnings reports, and enough time for the market to begin establishing how it values the stock.

Ionic Digital, , has less than a year of trading history. I’m not making a prediction about where the stock goes from here, it simply doesn’t have enough history to qualify for this ranking yet.

Before we continue… remember what we’re looking for: the stocks showing the highest probability of a significant move right now.

If I ranked your favorite stock lower, that doesn’t necessarily mean I think it’s a bad company, or even that the stock is going down. It simply means I found other tickers that currently fit my criteria better.

Have questions about a stock or why I ranked it where I did? Swing into the Main Chat and I’ll be happy to discuss more.

Weak Trend - Low Relative Strength

In this next elimination, I am seeking to get rid of the weakest trends, measured by Relative Strength. My personally built indicator (help yourself) has a feature that measures the asset’s performance against the S&P 500. Normally, stocks with the strongest, already developed trends, perform the best in major run ups.

Here is an example you see below Newsmax, . Don’t get me wrong, locally, I think it looks really bullish. But the relative strength is only 69. Why would I choose a stock that did not have trend strength in 2023? And 2024? And 2025? In a strong bull market…. Why is the stock down -86% from its highs? Could the stock go up? Absolutely. It is just not the most reliable asset in this list.

Because we had so many competitive stocks this episode, any stocks that had a relative strength score below 70, were eliminated. 21 more tickers have been crossed off.

Again, they could go up…but they are not the best choices today per my strategy.

Weakest Fundamentals

Many of the stocks eliminated here are still showing short-term uptrends that could continue. MicroStrategy, , is a good example.

We called for Bitcoin’s trend to continue on August 20. If Bitcoin continues higher, MSTR likely will benefit as well.

But that’s different from saying MSTR is one of the strongest stocks in this ranking. Its earnings profile does not meet the fundamental criteria I’m using here, so despite the potential for continued upside, it gets eliminated. Maybe Michael Saylor, MSTR and the Bitcoin Maxis make a fortune as BTC goes a trillion bajillion dollars. But that is a speculative gamble. Not a sound investment IMO.

There are other stocks that give me the combination of price action + fundamentals I’m looking for.

14 Stocks Remain

All 14 have passed the major tests: improving fundamentals, established uptrends, and strong relative strength.

At this stage, I’m not trying to identify good stocks. They’re all good stocks. I’m trying to identify which ones offer the best setup right now.

Too Parabolic - No Good SEPA

Our goal is to get into a winning position. If a stock has been going parabolic for weeks… then we are completely guessing where a top is at. How much further does it have? What we do know, is that the % profit potential has went down, and the % risk has went up. These are not situations we want to find ourself in. Okta Inc, has been performing really well. But the weekly chart is absolutely parabolic. No fresh breakouts.

Cloudflare, was the 22 July Mid-Week Mover winner. And to be fair, I am not seeing any warning signals with this one. However, our optimal specific point entry (SEPA) has passed. So what was once a winner, is now one to let run its course. Don’t go chasing rocket ship stocks!

Here’s another example. We ranked CrowdStrike #1 in June 2025. Since then, CRWD has gained roughly 110% from the area highlighted on the chart. That is exactly the type of move we’re trying to find now, not after the fact.

Subscribe now

But look at the difference between the setup then and the setup now.

Back then, we had an emerging fresh breakout with considerably more room for the trend to develop. Today, CRWD is dramatically extended from those levels. Could it continue higher? Absolutely.

But I don’t need to predict the top. I need to decide whether this is where I want to establish a new position. For this ranking, the answer is no.

NET and CRWD demonstrate what I’m trying to find before the huge move occurs. I’m not interested in putting a familiar winner back at #1 simply because its chart has continued higher.

I’m looking for the next setup.

That leaves us with 12 stocks out of the original 52.

What Separates the Final 12?

Now I’m getting extremely selective.

I’m looking for stocks where several things are lining up at the same time:

Strong fundamentals. Strong relative strength. An established uptrend. And, most importantly, a chart structure that still offers an attractive entry in SEPA range.

One setup I pay particular attention to is the Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP), p by Mark Minervini, 2-time U.S. Investing Champion. His approach is about 80% of my own strategy.

Rather than simply looking for a stock that’s moving higher, I’m looking for periods where volatility contracts and price tightens while the larger trend remains intact. You likely have heard me say it before… higher highs and higher lows, but no major breakout or run yet.

After starting with 52 stocks, eliminating the weak trends, removing companies that didn’t meet my fundamental criteria, and passing on previous winners that I believe are now too extended...

we’re down to 12.

And the stock sitting at #1 and #2 meets every major entry criteria I’m looking for.

Now, let’s rank the final 12...
